requirement.part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip

brief:
Part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip. Solid rectangular cross-section, width across the load, thickness in the load direction.
Load 2500 N at the tip, length 140 mm.
REQ-001 yield margin of safety >= 0 with factor 1.25 (MS = allowable / (factor x stress) - 1).
REQ-002 ultimate margin of safety >= 0 with factor 1.6.
REQ-003 tip deflection <= 3 mm.
REQ-004 width 10-60 mm, thickness 3-30 mm.
REQ-005 thickness must be a stock plate thickness: [3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 30] mm.
REQ-006 REQ-001 to REQ-003 must still hold with the load 10% higher and the plate 0.5 mm thinner.
REQ-007 thickness / width <= 2 (a proxy for lateral stability).
Materials: {"Al 6061-T6": {"density_kg_m3": 2700, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 68.9, "yield_mpa": 276.0, "ultimate_mpa": 310.0}, "Ti-6Al-4V": {"density_kg_m3": 4430, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 113.8, "yield_mpa": 880.0, "ultimate_mpa": 950.0}, "Steel 4130": {"density_kg_m3": 7850, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 205.0, "yield_mpa": 435.0, "ultimate_mpa": 670.0}}
Goal: the lowest mass that meets every requirement.

reasoning: Bending moment is M = PL = 350 N·m. Stress is 6PL/(b·h²), and tip deflection is 4PL³/(E·b·h³). Under the REQ-006 case (2750 N, effective thickness h−0.5), the ultimate allowable governs Al (193.75 MPa) and Ti (593.75 MPa), while the yield allowable governs steel (348 MPa). REQ-007 limits h/b ≤ 2. Rough sizing gives Ti-6Al-4V about 240 mm² (h=20, b=12), Al 6061 about 450 mm² (h=30, b=15), and Steel 4130 about 325 mm² (h=25, b=13). Mass also scales with density, so Ti is the likely lowest-mass choice. Specialists must verify each candidate against all requirements.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Ultimate governs at 310/1.6 = 193.75 MPa, and under REQ-006 (2750 N, t = h−0.5) stiffness needs b·t³ ≥ 1.46e5 mm³ and stress needs b·t² ≥ 1.19e4 mm², so search thick narrow sections near h = 25–30 mm and b = 15–20 mm (h/b ≤ 2).
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Ultimate governs at 950/1.6 = 593.75 MPa, which leaves large stress headroom, so stiffness is the binding limit; search h = 16–25 mm with b = 12–24 mm, where b·t³ ≥ 8.8e4 mm³ and b·t² ≥ 3.9e3 mm² under the REQ-006 case, with h = 20, b = 12 as the first candidate.
notes.Steel 4130: Yield governs at 435/1.25 = 348 MPa, and E = 205 GPa makes deflection easy, but its density of 7850 kg/m³ is about 1.8× Ti's, so search h = 20–25 mm with b = 13–18 mm only to confirm it cannot beat Ti on mass.

text: I'll start by checking three candidates across the stock thicknesses: 25 mm × 12.5 mm, 20 mm × 17.5 mm, and 16 mm × 28 mm.
I'll check the lightest candidates first. My hand estimates are based on sigma = 6M/(b·h²), δ = PL³/(3EI), and mass ≈ 0.378·b·h grams.
I'll start by checking the lead's first candidate (20 mm thick, 12 mm wide) alongside two other Ti-6Al-4V sizes that the stiffness and width/thickness limits point to.
The three candidates all pass. I'll check one more lighter boundary case and one more passing option to fill out the proposals.
The first three results match my hand calculations. The 12 × 20 mm design is the lightest so far, so I'll check two heavier neighbours to have verified alternatives.
The first three all pass, and the 25 × 12.5 mm design is the lightest so far. I'll check three more to round out the set of proposals.

The lightest passing Ti-6Al-4V design is 12 mm wide by 20 mm thick at 148.8 g. Stiffness under the REQ-006 case is the binding limit, as the lead expected. Five designs were checked in total, and all four proposals below pass every requirement, including the worst case.

| # | Width × thickness (mm) | Yield MS (est.) | Tip deflection (mm, est.) | Mass (g, est.) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12 × 2

The lightest passing Al 6061-T6 design is 15 × 30 mm at 170.1 g. I checked six designs in total; one failed REQ-006, which I've listed so the boundary is visible.

**Proposals (all pass every requirement, including REQ-006 and REQ-007)**

| # | Width b (mm) | Thickness t (mm) | Mass (g) | My yield MS | My tip deflection (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15 | 30 | 170.1 | +0.42 | 0.98 |
| 2 |

The lightest Steel 4130 design that passes every requirement is 12.5 mm wide by 25 mm thick, at about 343 g. I used six of the roughly ten checks. My hand calculations matched the tool's stresses, and deflection is never the limiting requirement for steel.

summary: The bracket passes all six structural rules (S-01 to S-06) and the material, form and fabrication checks M-02, M-03, M-04, F-01, F-02 and F-03, but M-01 remains action because it uses typical handbook values rather than alloy-, temper- and thickness-specific allowables. Open actions M-05, X-01, X-02, P-01, P-02 and P-03 must be closed before the design can be called compliant, and the status of P-04 is undetermined.
top_risks: M-01: Design allowables are typical handbook values, so the margins in S-01 to S-03 are not yet backed by MMPDS A- or B-basis data for this alloy, temper and thickness.
X-02: Fatigue is not analyzed, and no cyclic load cases such as launch vibration have been evaluated.
X-01: The fracture control classification is not recorded, which leaves the required rigor of the analysis and inspection undefined.

actions.action: Replace the typical values with MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for Ti-6Al-4V, the applicable temper and the 20 mm thickness, then rerun S-01 to S-03.
Define the cyclic load cases, including launch vibration, and perform the fatigue analysis.
Classify the part (for example non-fracture-critical) and record the rationale in the fracture control file.
Specify fastener material and finish at the Ti-6Al-4V joint to avoid galvanic corrosion, per MIL-STD-889.
Require a certificate of conformance and mill test report traceable to the heat lot before accepting the plate.

memo: Recommend awarding the order for 10 Ti-6Al-4V brackets to Vendor A (sample), which submitted a valid bid at $156.11 per part with an 18-day lead time and passed all eligibility checks with no flags, and was selected by the scoring that weights price at 0.6 and lead time at 0.4. Vendor B (sample) was not chosen because, although it quoted a lower price of $124.31 each, it was ruled ineligible and its bid was rejected since it does not work with Ti-6Al-4V, and its lead time was 23 days. Vendor C (sample) was not chosen because it submitted no bid and is ineligible for having no AS9100 quality system, and Vendor D (sample) was not chosen because it submitted no bid and is ineligible because it cannot certify a DFARS compliant melt source.
